description: Third-party forest management certifications a BC licensee can hold. The up-front cost is the system build and the registration audit; the annual cost is running the system (a certification coordinator, internal audits, the advisory group) and the auditors' fees, billed monthly. The premium is what certified fibre earns per m³ once the certificate is issued: small, because certification mostly buys market access. In the year it is booked a standard costs more than it earns; what it pays for is the certificate, the reputation and the buyers.

certifications.name: Forest Stewardship Council (FSC)
certifications.description: Most demanding standard, highest market premium; the Nation's consent provisions are part of the audit.

certifications.name: CSA Z809 (PEFC-endorsed)
certifications.description: The Canadian sustainable forest management standard; public advisory group, endorsed by PEFC for export markets.

certifications.name: Sustainable Forestry Initiative (SFI)
certifications.description: North American standard, the common entry point; annual surveillance audits.

mechanics.audit_compliance: The registration audit in May issues the certificate when every requirement is met; the premium and the reputation bonus start then. A failed registration gets a corrective-action request and one re-audit in October. A held certificate faces its surveillance audit in October.
mechanics.loss_penalty: A withdrawn application or a suspended certificate costs reputation, and a suspension also gives back the bonus the certificate earned.
mechanics.stacking: One standard per operating year: buyers pay for certified fibre once, whichever standard it carries.
